dedupe_keys.name: common alerting protocol cap version 1 2 oasis standard for all hazard emergency alerts and public warnings

description: The Common Alerting Protocol is the open message format used worldwide to send emergency alerts and public warnings, from weather and earthquake warnings to civil emergencies. Version 1.2 became an OASIS Standard in July 2010, building on CAP 1.1 from 2005. A CAP message says who sent the alert, its status and scope, the kind of event, its urgency, severity and certainty, instructions to the public and the affected area as polygons, circles or geocodes, so one warning can be pushed at the same time through sirens, broadcast, mobile and web channels. The specification is free to download from the OASIS document library as HTML, PDF or Word with its XML schema, and national profiles such as Australia's adapt it. Coverage is international; national alerting services in many countries publish CAP feeds. Caveats: a standard, not a dataset; the licence is the OASIS IPR policy, not an open data licence; national profiles add their own rules. Simulation uses: a common schema for injecting and reading warnings in evacuation and emergency response models, and for replaying historical alert feeds. Related records: CAP alert feeds are catalogued for the US National Weather Service (data-nws-cap-alerts), India (data-ndma-sachet-cap-alerts-india) and Taiwan (data-ncdr-taiwan-cap-public-alerts).
